history.description: A Special Educational Needs unit is established in the Ministry of Education
A school for learners with hearing impairments, now the Wangsel Institute, is established
The National Policy on Special Educational Needs demands mainstreaming of children with mild to moderate disabilities
The Bhutan Education Blueprint 2014-2024 addresses education for children with disabilities, with the emphasis on expanding special education
Standards for Inclusive Education are established, operationalising inclusion at school level
The National Policy for Persons with Disabilities defines disability on the social model

evidence.quote: Special Educational Needs unit established in Ministry of Education; child-friendly school practices emerging in schools
Established school for learners with hearing impairments (now known as Wangsel Institute)
It demands the “mainstreaming or integration of children with mild to moderate disabilities in regular schools with appropriate facilities and support services”
The Bhutan Education Blueprint 2014–2024 addresses education for children with disabilities, although the emphasis is on expanding special education
The Standards for Inclusive Education 2017 is a significant step in operationalizing the inclusion agenda, especially at the school level
Disability is defined based on the social model of disability in the National Policy for Persons with Disabilities 2019

sources.label: UNICEF ROSA, Mapping of Disability-Inclusive Education Practices in South Asia (2021), country profile: Bhutan — 'Milestones in disability-inclusive education' and Table 1 (Internet Archive copy)

history.description: The Maldives ratifies the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
The Protection of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and Provision of Financial Assistance Act 08/2010, the Disability Act, is enacted
Regulation 2011/R-3 is made under the Disability Act to govern protection of rights and financial assistance
An Inclusive Education Policy is formulated for the first time
Education Act 24/2020 prohibits any form of discrimination against persons with disabilities
The Inclusive Education Policy is revised, repositioning it from special needs to inclusive education
Regulation 2021/R-54 sets the criteria for determining and registering a person as disabled

evidence.quote: The Maldives ratified the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) in 2010
also known as the Disability Act) was enacted in 2010 following the ratification of the CRPD
regulations pertaining to the protection of the rights of persons with disabilities and providing financial assistance (2011/R-3)
The Inclusive Education Policy was first formulated in 2013 and was subsequently updated in 2021
Education Act (24/2020) Prohibits any form of discrimination against persons with disabilities
This revision marks a repositioning of the policy from special needs to inclusive education and a move away from the medical model
the determination and registry of persons with disabilities (2021/R-54) outline the criteria for individuals that can be registered as persons with disabilities

sources.label: United Nations Maldives, Situational Analysis of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in the Maldives — country report, sections on legislation, registration and inclusive education

history.description: The Ministry of Education establishes an Administration of Special Education
Article 56 of Education Law 1389 obliges the ministry to offer special education and care for disabled students
King Saud University opens the country's first undergraduate programme in speech-language pathology
The Disability Code is enacted, guaranteeing access to free and appropriate educational and rehabilitation services
Article 8 of the Disability Code calls for the creation of a Supreme Council for Disabled Affairs
Regulations of Special Education Programs and Institutes (RSEPI) introduced, reported as the first regulations for students with disabilities
Procedural regulations are issued to organise the institutes and programmes offering special education in the ministry
The Saudi Society of Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology is established

evidence.quote: The Ministry of Education established the Administration of Special Education in 1962
Article 56 of Education Law 1389 of 1970 states that the ministry is to offer special education and care
Since the first undergraduate program in SLP was established in 1985 at King Saud University
enacted in 2000 ‘to guarantee that people with disabilities have access to free and appropriate medical, psychological, social, educational, and rehabilitation services
Article 8 of the 2000 Disability Code calls for the creation of the Supreme Council for Disabled Affairs
The Regulations of Special Education Programs and Institutes (RSEPI) were modelled after those U.S. policies and introduced in 2001
Article 2 of the 2002 procedural regulations to organize institutes and programmes offering special education in the Ministry of Education
The Saudi Society of Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology (SSSPA) was established in 2005

history.description: The Ministry of Education establishes a unit dedicated to inclusion in education
Law No. 34 of 2004 art. 9(1) obliges the state to give full care for the education of children with disabilities
Ministerial Decree No. 515 presses for integration of students with special needs in public schools
The National Plan for Disability 2008-25 makes integrating children with disabilities in schools a priority
Legislative Decree No. 12 of 10 February ratifies the CRPD and its Optional Protocol
Law No. 7 of 2012 art. 2(d) refers students with severe disability to the Ministry of Social Affairs
The Ministry of Health opens four newborn clinics in three governorates for early identification of disabilities

evidence.quote: In 2000, the Ministry of Education established a unit dedicated to inclusion in education
Article 9(1) of Law No. 34 of 2004 states that the state is to give full care for the education of children with disabilities
Ministerial Decree No. 515 of 2006 highlights the importance of integrating students with special needs with the other students in public schools
the 2008–25 National Plan for Disability sets a priority to help integrate children with disabilities in schools
By Legislative Decree No. 12, promulgated on 10 February 2009 (Annex 49), Syria ratified the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
Article 2(d) of Law No. 7 of 2012 stipulates that students with severe cases of disability are to be referred
the Ministry of Health opened four clinics for newborn infants in three governorates (Damascus, Homs and Tartus) for early identification of disabilities

sources.label: UNESCO GEM Report, Profiles Enhancing Education Reviews (PEER), Syrian Arab Republic: Inclusion — sections 'School Organization', 'Integration', 'Disability' and 'Governance'

history.description: Diagnosis and correction of communication disorders begins as a hospital service at Ramathibodi Hospital
Master's courses are opened in audiology and in speech-language pathology
The Thai Speech-Language and Hearing Association is formally registered on 6 October
National Education Act B.E. 2542 gives persons with communication deficiencies a right to specially provided basic education
Practitioners are required to sit a registration examination for a licence as practitioners of the healing arts
Persons with Disabilities Empowerment Act B.E. 2550 revokes the Act on Rehabilitation of Persons with Disabilities B.E. 2534
The same Act counts impairment in communication among the impairments that make a person disabled
Education Provision for Persons with Disabilities Act B.E. 2551 gives a right to education without cost from birth or from discovery of the disability
The same Act creates a fund for the promotion and development of education for persons with disabilities
